name: ALTER EGO
tagline: A free-to-play IPL fantasy cricket app with private leagues, an 11-player team builder and live scores, now fronted by the ALTER EGO sports desk landing page.
problem: Friends who follow the IPL want a private way to pick fantasy teams for each match and compare results without entry fees or payouts. HITMAN started as that app; the Phase 0 rework removed money flows, random scoring and mock data, and added an ALTER EGO landing page for a planned multi-sport sports desk and prediction game.
how: The landing page explains the ALTER EGO concept and runs a Make the Call demo: pick a decision in a frozen match moment, lock it in and see how a toy model graded the call.
Visitors can browse the IPL 2026 schedule of 70 league matches, all ten squads with captains and coaches, and a points table snapshot.
After registering with email and password (NextAuth credentials), a user creates a private league with an invite code or joins one with a 6-digit code.
The league lobby lists live and upcoming matches; JOIN CONTEST opens the team builder for that fixture.

The builder enforces 11 players, a 100 credit cap and role limits (3 to 6 batters and bowlers, 1 to 4 all-rounders, 1 to 3 wicketkeepers), then asks for a captain (2x points) and vice-captain (1.5x points).
The server re-validates the team with the same shared rules, closes selection once a match leaves UPCOMING, and shows the locked-in XI.
features: Private leagues with cryptographically random invite codes
Team builder with role filters, credits left and team progress bars
Captain and vice-captain multipliers from a versioned scoring config
Full IPL 2026 schedule and squads for all ten franchises
Live score centre fed by CricketData.org, with a clear message when no API key is set
Admin-only seed, score and toss routes
ALTER EGO landing page with The Desk brief, Make the Call demo, roster and alter ego file
ai: There is no LLM in the running app; the Make the Call demo on the landing page uses illustrative data and a toy model, as the page itself states.
The multi-sport AI sports desk described on the landing page is a planned direction, not implemented yet.

stack.frontend: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide icons
stack.backend: Next.js route handlers, NextAuth credentials auth with bcryptjs
stack.ai: None in the app; toy model on the landing demo

run: cp .env.example .env (set DATABASE_URL and NEXTAUTH_SECRET), npm install, npx prisma generate && npx prisma db push, npm run dev
notes: Ran locally as a production build against a local PostgreSQL 16 on port 5333, seeded with the repo's scripts/seed-2026.ts (real IPL 2026 squads and schedule; the seed generates random historical player stats and credits). The seed sets match status from the current date, and since the 2026 season is over every match would be COMPLETED with an empty lobby, so the seed was run with its clock set to 20 April 2026, which left 31 matches completed, 2 live and 37 upcoming. The account, league and team were created through the real UI. No CRICKET_API_KEY was set, so the live score panels show the app's own not configured message. No points were scored, so the leaderboard shows 0. A local .env was added; no code was changed. The video was sped up by 10 percent to fit the time limit.
